title: Knowledge Check 2: Lessons 9-16
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 9-16 of the agentic-ai series. Score 80% or higher to progress toward the practice exam.

questions.question: Per the lesson “Function-Calling Parity Across OpenAI, Azure, Anthropic, Gemini, and Local Models”, what is the central focus?
options: Every frontier provider exposes function calling, but none uses the same wire format.
A history of the technology and its vendors
A review of unrelated productivity tools
A summary of corporate policy rules
questions.explanation: The lesson is centered on: Every frontier provider exposes function calling, but none uses the same wire format. This lesson maps the request and response shapes across OpenAI, Azure, Anthropic, and Gemini, then shows why local models (llama.cpp) are the parity wildcard and how one internal schema plus thin per-provider adapters keeps an agent portable.

questions.question: Per the lesson “Agent Memory: Short-Term vs Long-Term, Episodic vs Semantic”, what is the central focus?
options: An agent with no memory answers the same question the same way forever.
A history of the technology and its vendors

questions.explanation: The lesson is centered on: An agent with no memory answers the same question the same way forever. This lesson maps the memory taxonomy production systems borrow from cognitive science: the context window as working memory, long-term stores for persistence, episodic memory for what happened, semantic memory for what you know, and the pipeline that turns raw interactions into retrievable knowledge.

questions.question: Per the lesson “Multi-Turn Agents: Sessions, State, and Resuming Conversations”, what is the central focus?
options: An LLM is stateless: every call forgets the one before it, so multi-turn behavior has to be built, not assumed.

questions.explanation: The lesson is centered on: An LLM is stateless: every call forgets the one before it, so multi-turn behavior has to be built, not assumed. This lesson defines the session, the state it carries, and the checkpointing that lets an agent resume where it left off: the difference between a thread and a durable store, why the state schema is the real design, and how production systems survive restarts and long conversations.
